text:
kevin_support: Heads up — Walletly is getting repeated 429s and big latency spikes on Dedicated pool eu-west-1. Customer reports app-level errors and timeout retries. Seen this twice in the last 90m. Can someone triage? :rotating_light:

alex_sre: Checking autoscale logs and the request telemetry now. Any repro steps from support?

kevin_support: Minimal repro — their integration does bursty batch imports every ~5m, each job opens ~300 concurrent reqs to /v1/generate. They say it was fine yesterday. They attached a sample curl: `curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H 'Authorization: Bearer <token>' -d '{"prompt":"...","max_tokens":512}'` and timestamps.

maya_oncall: Pasting autoscaler event stream for the pool (redacted):
```
2024-10-21T09:10:12Z autoscale-bot: scaling up pool-ded-eu-7 -> +8 GPUs (reason: avg_queue_ms>1500)
2024-10-21T09:12:03Z autoscale-bot: scaling down pool-ded-eu-7 -> -6 GPUs (reason: idle_shrink)
2024-10-21T09:14:41Z autoscale-bot: scaling up pool-ded-eu-7 -> +7 GPUs (reason: avg_queue_ms>1600)
2024-10-21T09:16:20Z autoscale-bot: scaling down pool-ded-eu-7 -> -9 GPUs (reason: cooldown_expired)
```
Feels like a classic oscillation — scale up then quick shrink. Current cooldown is 60s and target_latency threshold looks aggressive.

alex_sre: Can you attach the metric time-series for `queue_ms`, `inflight_requests`, and `instance_count` for that window? Also need the tenant config (burst allowance).

maya_oncall: Uploaded short graph to staff dash: https://dash.internal/redwood/pool-ded-eu-7?range=30m (private). Quick take: `inflight_requests` spikes correlate with their import job and then queue_ms decays, but `instance_count` trails and then overshoots downward.

autoscale-bot: [automated] pool-ded-eu-7 cooldown_seconds=60, min_instances=3, max_instances=80, scale_step=8

kevin_support: Customer also saw intermittent 401s mixed in with 429s — digging, but earlier looked like token refresh flapping on their side. Might be increasing retry storms.

alex_sre: Two immediate mitigations I recommend: 1) raise cooldown_seconds to 300 for that pool to damp oscillation; 2) reduce `scale_step` to 3-4 to avoid big overshoot. We should also add a short-lived prefix cache for that tenant while we stabilize.

dan_product: If we change cooldown, do we need a customer heads-up? Could affect burst capacity for them. Also watch billing implications if we hold more nodes longer.

maya_oncall: I'll patch the pool config in staging and run a 30m A/B between cooldown=60 and cooldown=300, keeping an eye on 95p latency and queue_ms. If results look good, we'll roll to prod for that pool only.

kevin_support: Customer on call in 20m. Suggest we do the quick staging run and then apply to prod if it calms down. I'll tell them we're investigating and may throttle their burst or request they spread imports.

alex_sre: Also adding a quick guard: cap per-tenant concurrency to 200 on that pool as a temporary noisy-neighbor mitigation. We'll surface a followup doc for permanent quota controls.

maya_oncall: Test patch applied to staging config. Command used: `redwoodctl pool update pool-ded-eu-7 --cooldown-seconds=300 --scale-step=4 --tenant-concurrency-cap=200`

autoscale-bot: [automated] staging: applied config change to pool-ded-eu-7 (cooldown_seconds=300, scale_step=4)

alex_sre: After 30m staging run: oscillations reduced, instance_count smoother, queue_ms 95p dropped ~35%. Recommend prod change and a transient tenant cap retention of 2 hours.

dan_product: Approving targeted prod change and customer communication. Mention we'll revert tenant cap once they fix client retry/backoff.

kevin_support: I'll update Walletly. Thanks team. Will monitor and re-open if anything else pops up. :thumbsup:

autoscale-bot: [automated] prod: applied config change to pool-ded-eu-7 (cooldown_seconds=300, scale_step=4, tenant_concurrency-cap=200)

maya_oncall: Monitoring alerts set: notify @oncall if scale actions > 3 in 10m or queue_ms 95p > 2000ms.

kevin_support: Customer confirmed errors reduced after change. Closing for now but logging runbook items: - default cooldown tuning per pool - rapid tenant concurrency mitigation steps - ops checklist for noisy tenant escalations
